text:
jordan: dropping the nsys from the 2pm staging run — latency regression linked to a burst of queue_time spikes. TL;DR: big KV-cache sweep aligns with kernel switchover and a train of small batches that thrash matmul launches. anyone seen this pattern before?

jordan: command i ran: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=cpu ./staging_infer --model=rwkv-16b --seq=2048 --batchsize=1`

jordan: top slice from timeline (copied):
```
GPU timeline:
- 00:00.000 - kernel: kv_prefetch (3.2ms)
- 00:00.003 - kernel: matmul_1 (1.1ms)
- 00:00.004 - kernel: matmul_2 (0.9ms)
- 00:00.005 - kernel: kv_sweep (4.8ms)  <-- big
- 00:00.010 - kernel: matmul_3 (1.0ms)
Queue times spike to 6-8ms right before kv_sweep.
```

maya: ugh that looks like the KV cache's sweep thread migrating work to a different CU and invalidating prefetched blocks. saw something similar when we changed the prefetch window to 256 tokens.

maya: quick note: the trace shows `kv_sweep` runs on stream 3 while matmuls are on stream 0, but there's a sync fence between them. so compute waits. :confused: could be kernel affinity or our fallback quantized kernel touching same memory region.

li: pinging with an experiment idea: bind kv_sweep to a low-priority stream and change kernel selection so prefetch uses `kern_pref_v2` (smaller regs, shorter occupancy). that should reduce sweep tail. also try lowering continuous_batch.window from 8ms -> 4ms to avoid collecting lots of tiny requests into a single sweeping event.

sam: perfetto link: https://perfetto.example/runs/1755556677 (contains full CPU/GPU slice). my hot take: queue_time dominates for ~2.3s windows; compute is stable. looks like backpressure from the cache-only ops.

sam: quick snippet from perf counters: `dram_read_bytes` jumps by 3x during kv_sweep, and `sm_efficiency` drops ~22% for the next two kernels.

perf-bot: automated-summary: GPU busy 78%, idle 12%, kernel_stalls 9%. Frequent kernel launches: matmul (80%), kv_prefetch (9%), kv_sweep (6%). Correlation: kv_sweep start correlates with queue spike (r=0.67).

jordan: thanks. i reproduced locally with `--kv-prefetch=on --continuous-window-ms=8` and see same spike. attaching small flame snippet in case it helps: https://blob.example/flame/1755556677.json

maya: can we try two quick experiments on staging: 1) pin kv_sweep to stream 5 + low priority and 2) force kernel selection to `kern_pref_v2` for prefetch. if spikes go away we know it's kernel/memory interference.

li: i'll run 1) now. scheduling a deploy to canary with `KERNEL_AFFINITY=5 KV_SWEEP_PRIORITY=low` — will post results in ~3m.

sam: also try reducing `continuous_batch.max_delay_ms` to 4 in the same canary to observe batching behavior. if batching window is too long we merge many small requests that cause frequent sweeps.

li: canary run finished: queue_time median down 35%, kv_sweep still present but tail reduced (was 4.8ms -> 1.6ms). matmul latency slightly up by 0.2ms but total P95 reduced.

maya: promising. that suggests interference more than algorithmic regressions. low-priority sweep lets compute go first.

jordan: great. next steps: 1) roll low-priority kv_sweep change to staging for 6h smoke, 2) prepare a kernel selection fallback (kern_pref_v2) + perf test, 3) add a trace-guard that captures nsys when queue_time P90 > 5ms in prod.

sam: +1. i'll add the trace-guard PR and a small perf dashboard showing kv_sweep frequency vs batch_window.

perf-bot: action logged: trace-guard created (#3482). scheduled nsys retention 72h for flagged runs.

jordan: thanks all. leaving steps in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-8123 — i'll follow up with benchmarks after 6h canary. :thumbsup:

li: FYI, observed one regression case where forcing `kern_pref_v2` increases CPU-side launch overhead slightly; will quantify.

maya: cool. if `kern_pref_v2` hurts launch overhead we might instead use dynamic threshold: pref_v2 only when seq_len >= 1024 or when batchsize>1.

jordan: sounds good. stopping trace capture for now. thanks folks.
